description:
Found by the fz-kdt.198 refutation (2026-09-03). PRE-EXISTING: identical at
accb5cfbe, at 198's c1f7a7d1b and at its fold. Every `case` written over a
variable bound to a binary literal whose arms include a non-binary pattern
(an integer literal, an atom, a list) crashes the interpreter with
`fz2 interp: backend value 3 is unbound` instead of taking the binary arm or
diagnosing the dead arm. It is the reason no source-level reproducer exists
for 198's residue (fz-kdt.203) or for the union-hull regression 198's refuter
found at the calculator: cross-kind narrowing from source cannot be
exercised. Reproducer (r4_lit_pattern_join.fz, also r6/r7 list variants in
the 198 research archive):

import Utf8

defmodule M do
  @spec take(utf8) :: integer
  fn take(_x), do: 1
end

fn main() do
  b = <<104, 105>>
  s = Utf8.from_bytes!(b)
  x = case b do
    1 -> s
    _ -> s
  end
  dbg(M.take(x))
end

Board neighbours: fz-9in (closed; "backend value 0 is unbound" on Enum.take
beside an unused range binding) and fz-xvq (closed; interp value unbound on
bsx guards) are the same symptom class -- an unbound backend value is a
lowering that referenced a slot no arm materialised. Red-first: the fixture
prints its binary arm on three doors; a dead cross-kind arm is a
type/no-matching-clause warning, not a crash.
title: [BUG] interp dies "backend value 3 is unbound" on a `case` over a <<>>-bound variable with a cross-kind pattern arm
